title: Carrier Management Process Summary: Functionality

children:
- Carrier Management controls how all facets of carrier assignment and 
 shipping will be executed in your warehouse.

- You can create routing guides, which identify which carrier, or carrier 
 group, can transport product for a specific customer or company. You can 
 define these routing guides per weight range and/or number of containers. 
 For example, this would be helpful if you want to route larger shipments 
 to LTL carriers and smaller ones to parcel carriers.

- You can create shipping calendars, which identify days that a carrier, 
 or group of carriers, cannot ship product. You can set no ship days for 
 either specific dates, like holidays, or for Saturday and/or Sunday.

- To minimize setup time, you can create one standard carrier record and 
 inherit those values to subsequent records. For example, you could create 
 one record for UPS that identifies the carrier's SCAC Code and corporate 
 address. You would then inherit these shared values on the records you 
 create for UPS' services. This is especially helpful if a carrier offers 
 multiple services.

- The system can estimate the number of containers on a shipment during 
 the wave. It will use this information to rate the carriers during the 
 wave.

- Most accessorials for UPS and FedEx are predefined for you. You can 
 create additional accessorials to support either these carriers or other 
 carriers that you use.
The following are key features of the allocation functional area:

Routing and rating determine which 
 carrier will transport a shipment. They are run during a wave. 
 First, routing determines if a particular routing guide should be applied 
 to a shipment. If a routing guide should be applied to the shipment, the 
 system will assign the carrier on the guide to the shipment.

If a carrier group is defined on the 
 guide, the system will rate all carriers in the group. It will 
 then assign the cheapest carrier to the shipment. If a routing guide was 
 applied to the shipment, rating will calculate the how much it will cost 
 to transport the shipment with the carrier defined on the guide.

If a routing guide was not applied 
 to the shipment, rating will select a carrier based on costs. The 
 cheapest carrier that can deliver the package is selected during rating 
 (when no routing guide is applied).

Progistics CS is an external rating system that supplies carrier rates 
 to the system. It also generates all shipping labels and parcel manifests. You can access the Progistics application directly on the application desktop.

When you install Progistics CS on your server, it includes the following: 
 a Progistics Software Server, the Progistics Manager Software, and a Software 
 Rate Server for each carrier that you use (and Progistics CS supports). 
 These Software Rate Servers are installed on your site's server. This 
 allows you to perform all manifesting activity onsite: your server will 
 never need to communicate across the intranet or with any device not onsite. 
 This maximizes processing time and ensures that you are not dependent 
 on external systems for your rates.

When you create records on particular system configurations, such as 
 the Shipper Code Window, the system communicates that information to the 
 Progistics Software Server and the Progistics Manager Software. When you 
 manifest a container with a particular carrier, the Software Rate Server 
 for that carrier assigns a rate and tracking number to the parcel.

Please note that FedEx does require a physical application server, which 
 is located at your site. To streamline the example, UPS is used to represent 
 all non-FedEx carriers, since all other carriers use the same server setup.

The system communicates to the 
 appropriate Progistics server components to either convey configuration 
 information or manifest a container:

When 
 someone maintains a record on any of the following configurations, 
 the system communicates this update to the Progistics Software Server 
 and the Progistics Manager Software:

Please note that these records are originally setup before you 
 can manifest containers. However, you can create, edit and delete these 
 records when you want. If you access the Progistics CS web page, you might 
 configure some of these values. For example, you will need to register 
 the shippers that you defined on the Shipper Code Window. Note that this 
 web page is not an external website. It is actually maintained on either 
 the Progistics Software Server or the Progistics Manager Software.

When 
 the system transmits a manifest request to the Software Server. 
 This manifest request includes the following information about the container: 
 shipment number, carrier and service, container weight, ship date, ship 
 to name and address, and other values required for processing.

If this carrier is FedEx, 
 continue to a. If this carrier is NOT FedEx, continue to step 2.

The FedEx Rate Server Software transmits the manifest request 
 to the FedEx PowerShip Server. This is a physical server that is located 
 at your site, but owned and maintained by Federal Express.

The FedEx PowerShip Server processes the 
 request. It transmits the manifest information, rate and tracking number 
 back to the FedEx Rate Server Software. Continue to Step 2.

The Progistics component sends a response 
 back to the system.

If configuration information was passed during Step 1, the Progistics 
 Services Server and Manager Software will communicate to the system that 
 a record was updated or maintained.

If manifesting was attempted during Step 1, 
 the Server Software communicates manifesting information to the system, 
 which stores relevant fields on the container. When necessary, the system 
 retrieves the manifest information from the Server Software.

LTL rating is performed within the SCALE system. The freight charge for these shipments is calculated by taking the total weight of the shipment, the final destination and the makeup of the product in the shipment. The makeup of the shipment is broken down into LTL classes. The rate charged is typically lower per pounds for items with lower LTL freight classes. The rate is also determined by the distance traveled.  Once all of the carriers and rate base configurations have been defined, the regular rating processing takes place.

Manifesting associates a container with a carrier's parcel manifest. 
 Only containers associated with a parcel carrier are manifested. When 
 a container is packed and closed, the system may automatically manifest 
 it (based on user's packing preference record). Containers can be manually 
 manifested on the Shipping Container Insight screen.

During manifesting, the system transmits container specific information, 
 such as its weight, carrier and carrier service, to Progistics CS. Progistics 
 CS contacts the carrier's server and manifests the container. It also 
 retrieves the container's tracking number and its rate. Progistics CS 
 transmits this information to the system. The system displays this information 
 on the Manifest Insight Screen and on the shipment line record. From 
 a user perspective, this process is seamless and very fast.

You can remanifest a container as often as you want, until the manifest 
 is closed.

This value is defined by the system and displayed on the Shipping Container 
 screen. It identifies the manifest state of the container.

Blank - No manifesting attempts 
 have been committed. The container has not been manifested.

Error - At least one manifest 
 attempt was committed and the container could not be manifested.

Manifested - The container 
 was successfully manifested. It has been associated with a carrier's manifest. 
 The container has a tracking ID and rate.

Closed 
 - The container was manifested and shipped. Once a manifest is closed, 
 containers on that manifested cannot be changed or removed from the manifest.

Freight bills can be assigned to the customer, a 3rd party, your warehouse 
 or a company within your warehouse. The system assigns freight bills based 
 on how you have configured the system. Below is a description of how the 
 system determines who pays the freight bill.

The system obtains the freight term from the shipment. If a freight 
 term is not defined, the system assigns the Prepaid term. It checks the 
 corresponding freight term record in the application. If the Shipper Pays 
 Freight? Checkbox is selected for this freight term, the system will assign 
 the shipping cost to the warehouse or a company within it.

If you 
 support multi-company processing, the system will attempt 
 to assign the shipping costs to the company who provided the product. 
 If the Freight Bill To Tab on the company record contains a bill to address, 
 the system assigns the shipping cost to the company. If this tab is blank, 
 the system will assign the shipping costs to the warehouse.

If you do not support multi-company processing or a company 
 is not associated with this shipment, the system will assign 
 the freight costs to the warehouse.

If the Shipper Pays Freight? Checkbox is not selected, 
 the system checks the shipment record. If values are defined on 
 the freight bill to tab, the system will assign the shipping costs to 
 the party identified here. If this tab is blank, the system will reference 
 the customer tab. If values are defined on the customer tab, that party 
 is assigned the freight bill. If no values are defined on the customer 
 tab, the system will bill the ship to name and address for the freight 
 costs.

Some carriers are not directly supported by 
 the current SCALE rating system. Therefore, the application provides some 
 generic functionality that can be used to rate shipments using any carrier 
 that you desire. This functionality includes generic paperwork documents 
 that allow container information to be generated for any carrier, as well 
 as interface uploads (in XML format to the Enterprise Integration Services 
 application) that can be used to send data back to any carrier.

To handle the container data uploads, the 
 system places the Billing Management data into an output XML file which can be retrieved by the carrier's system. Certain carriers require 
 to be sent to them a document that displays all of the containers that 
 were shipped for a certain day. The system meets this requirement by generating 
 an XML Container List which represents all of the containers on a shipping load, 
 or all containers for a certain day. The system will place this document 
 into the Billing Management output folder on the application server.

Rate shopping allows you to view potential 
 carriers and their rate charges before assigning a carrier to a shipment. 
 Unlike routing, rate shopping is an interactive process that is initiated 
 by the user per shipment. You can also rate shop against a country/postal 
 code combination before an actual shipment is created. This allows you 
 to give a customer the best delivery option even before an order is placed.

Once you analyze the results of your rate 
 search, you can assign a new carrier for your shipment, or choose to keep 
 the existing carrier. Note that you can rate shop any shipment in any 
 status (except shipments that are in an "in process" wave or 
 have been ship confirmed). SCALE uses a web service to calculate the rates 
 and display them on the Rate Shopping Window.

SCALE only allows you to rate shop for carriers 
 that the application currently supports. The system will only consider 
 carriers that have system calculated rates (as defined on the Carrier 
 Window). Carriers with manually-assigned rates or no rates are not included 
 in rate shopping.

UPS World Ease is a carrier service that expedites 
 the shipping of product to international destinations. It allows for quick 
 movement through the border customs process, and delivery to an intermediate 
 consignee (a hub, for example), which quickly processes packages before 
 shipping them to their final destination. View 
 this

to see a more 
 detailed look of the World Ease process flow:

World Ease shipments are packed using a special 
 type of shipping label that is affixed each shipping container. These 
 labels include the ship to address for both the intermediate consignee 
 (a hub) and the final shipping destination. Also included with the shipping 
 containers is a separate "document box," which contains the 
 appropriate paperwork that World Ease requires to ship the packages over 
 the border and into the hub destination.

SCALE uses "World Ease groups" to 
 represent the container(s) whose final destination is the same intermediate 
 consignee. The system assigns a container to a group during the container 
 manifesting process. When a group is closed, you will be able to print 
 the appropriate World Ease documentation, which includes a

special 
 box label, consolidated invoice, certificate of origin, and master invoice.

If configuration information was passed during Step 1, the Progistics 
 Services Server and Manager Software will communicate to the system that 
 a record was updated or maintained.

                    
 

                

                
If manifesting was attempted during Step 1, 
 the Server Software communicates manifesting information to the system, 
 which stores relevant fields on the container. When necessary, the system 
 retrieves the manifest information from the Server Software.

            

        

        
 

        
 

        
LTL Rating

        
LTL rating is performed within the SCALE system. The freight charge for these shipments is calculated by taking the total weight of the shipment, the final destination and the makeup of the product in the shipment. The makeup of the shipment is broken down into LTL classes. The rate charged is typically lower per pounds for items with lower LTL freight classes. The rate is also determined by the distance traveled.  Once all of the carriers and rate base configurations have been defined, the regular rating processing takes place. 

        
 

        
 

        
 

        
Manifesting

        
Manifesting associates a container with a carrier's parcel manifest. 
 Only containers associated with a parcel carrier are manifested. When 
 a container is packed and closed, the system may automatically manifest 
 it (based on user's packing preference record). Containers can be manually 
 manifested on the Shipping Container Insight screen.

        
 

        
During manifesting, the system transmits container specific information, 
 such as its weight, carrier and carrier service, to Progistics CS. Progistics 
 CS contacts the carrier's server and manifests the container. It also 
 retrieves the container's tracking number and its rate. Progistics CS 
 transmits this information to the system. The system displays this information 
 on the Manifest Insight Screen and on the shipment line record. From 
 a user perspective, this process is seamless and very fast.

        
 

        
You can remanifest a container as often as you want, until the manifest 
 is closed.

        
 

        
Manifest 
 Statuses
        

        
This value is defined by the system and displayed on the Shipping Container 
 screen. It identifies the manifest state of the container.

        

            

                
Blank - No manifesting attempts 
 have been committed. The container has not been manifested.

                
 

            

            

                
Error - At least one manifest 
 attempt was committed and the container could not be manifested.

                
 

            

            

                
Manifested - The container 
 was successfully manifested. It has been associated with a carrier's manifest. 
 The container has a tracking ID and rate.

                
 

            

            
Closed 
 - The container was manifested and shipped. Once a manifest is closed, 
 containers on that manifested cannot be changed or removed from the manifest.

        

        
 

        
 

        
How Freight Bills Are Assigned

        
Freight bills can be assigned to the customer, a 3rd party, your warehouse 
 or a company within your warehouse. The system assigns freight bills based 
 on how you have configured the system. Below is a description of how the 
 system determines who pays the freight bill.

        

            

                
The system obtains the freight term from the shipment. If a freight 
 term is not defined, the system assigns the Prepaid term. It checks the 
 corresponding freight term record in the application. If the Shipper Pays 
 Freight? Checkbox is selected for this freight term, the system will assign 
 the shipping cost to the warehouse or a company within it.

                
 

            

            

                

                    
If you 
 support multi-company processing, the system will attempt 
 to assign the shipping costs to the company who provided the product. 
 If the Freight Bill To Tab on the company record contains a bill to address, 
 the system assigns the shipping cost to the company. If this tab is blank, 
 the system will assign the shipping costs to the warehouse.

                    
 

                

                
If you do not support multi-company processing or a company 
 is not associated with this shipment, the system will assign 
 the freight costs to the warehouse.

            

            
 

            
If the Shipper Pays Freight? Checkbox is not selected, 
 the system checks the shipment record. If values are defined on 
 the freight bill to tab, the system will assign the shipping costs to 
 the party identified here. If this tab is blank, the system will reference 
 the customer tab. If values are defined on the customer tab, that party 
 is assigned the freight bill. If no values are defined on the customer 
 tab, the system will bill the ship to name and address for the freight 
 costs.

        

        
 

        
 

        
Carrier Compliance

        
Some carriers are not directly supported by 
 the current SCALE rating system. Therefore, the application provides some 
 generic functionality that can be used to rate shipments using any carrier 
 that you desire. This functionality includes generic paperwork documents 
 that allow container information to be generated for any carrier, as well 
 as interface uploads (in XML format to the Enterprise Integration Services 
 application) that can be used to send data back to any carrier.

        
 

        
To handle the container data uploads, the 
 system places the Billing Management data into an output XML file which can be retrieved by the carrier's system. Certain carriers require 
 to be sent to them a document that displays all of the containers that 
 were shipped for a certain day. The system meets this requirement by generating 
 an XML Container List which represents all of the containers on a shipping load, 
 or all containers for a certain day. The system will place this document 
 into the Billing Management output folder on the application server. 

        
 

        
 

        
 

        
 

        
Rate Shopping

        
Rate shopping allows you to view potential 
 carriers and their rate charges before assigning a carrier to a shipment. 
 Unlike routing, rate shopping is an interactive process that is initiated 
 by the user per shipment. You can also rate shop against a country/postal 
 code combination before an actual shipment is created. This allows you 
 to give a customer the best delivery option even before an order is placed. 
 

        
 

        
Once you analyze the results of your rate 
 search, you can assign a new carrier for your shipment, or choose to keep 
 the existing carrier. Note that you can rate shop any shipment in any 
 status (except shipments that are in an "in process" wave or 
 have been ship confirmed). SCALE uses a web service to calculate the rates 
 and display them on the Rate Shopping Window. 

        
 

        
SCALE only allows you to rate shop for carriers 
 that the application currently supports. The system will only consider 
 carriers that have system calculated rates (as defined on the Carrier 
 Window). Carriers with manually-assigned rates or no rates are not included 
 in rate shopping.

        
 

        
 

        
 

        
UPS World Ease

        
UPS World Ease is a carrier service that expedites 
 the shipping of product to international destinations. It allows for quick 
 movement through the border customs process, and delivery to an intermediate 
 consignee (a hub, for example), which quickly processes packages before 
 shipping them to their final destination. View 
 this diagram to see a more 
 detailed look of the World Ease process flow:

        
 

        
World Ease shipments are packed using a special 
 type of shipping label that is affixed each shipping container. These 
 labels include the ship to address for both the intermediate consignee 
 (a hub) and the final shipping destination. Also included with the shipping 
 containers is a separate "document box," which contains the 
 appropriate paperwork that World Ease requires to ship the packages over 
 the border and into the hub destination. 

        
 

        
SCALE uses "World Ease groups" to 
 represent the container(s) whose final destination is the same intermediate 
 consignee. The system assigns a container to a group during the container 
 manifesting process. When a group is closed, you will be able to print 
 the appropriate World Ease documentation, which includes a special 
 box label, consolidated invoice, certificate of origin, and master invoice.
